entries.summary: Choose Databricks-managed compute for this pipeline.
details: With serverless off, supply a clusters configuration. Classic-only options such as edition and photon are ignored for serverless pipelines.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit project defaults; if neither level sets it, LHP uses true.

entries.summary: Select the pipeline edition for classic compute.
details: CORE, PRO and ADVANCED are the accepted values. This field is omitted from the generated pipeline resource when serverless is enabled.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit project defaults; LHP’s built-in edition is ADVANCED.

entries.summary: Choose the pipeline runtime release channel.
details: Use CURRENT for the stable channel or PREVIEW when deliberately evaluating upcoming runtime features.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit project defaults; LHP’s built-in channel is CURRENT.

entries.summary: Control whether the pipeline keeps running between updates.
details: This is a pipeline execution setting. It is separate from an action’s readMode, which chooses how that action reads data.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit project defaults; LHP’s built-in setting is false.

entries.summary: Choose how the generated pipeline code is shipped.
details: source ships source files; wheel builds a Python wheel and requires wheel.artifact_volume in lhp.yaml.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit project defaults; only when neither level specifies packaging does LHP use source.

choices.explanation: Build and upload a Python wheel.

entries.summary: Choose the Unity Catalog catalog for this pipeline’s tables.
details: Enter a literal name or a substitution token. Both catalog and schema must resolve to nonempty values for bundle generation.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit the project-default catalog; no usable value means bundle generation cannot proceed.

entries.summary: Choose the Unity Catalog schema for this pipeline’s tables.
details: Enter a literal name or a substitution token. Both schema and catalog must resolve to nonempty values for bundle generation.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit the project-default schema; no usable value means bundle generation cannot proceed.

entries.summary: Pass named string settings to the pipeline.
details: Every value in this mapping must be a string, including numbers and booleans. Nested mappings merge with defaults by key.

entries.summary: Declare the runtime environment used by the pipeline.
details: Use dependencies for pip requirement specifiers needed by pipeline code; the environment mapping is passed to the generated pipeline resource.
entries.unsetBehavior: When unset here, the project-default value applies. If neither level sets this key, only a documented LHP or platform default applies; omission is not the same as an explicit value.

entries.summary: Install Python requirements needed by pipeline code.
details: List pip requirement specifiers such as requests==2.32.3. A locally declared list replaces the inherited list rather than appending to it.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit the dependency list from project defaults.

entries.summary: Configure classic compute when serverless is disabled.
details: Enter pipeline cluster definitions. This list is required for classic compute and replaces an inherited list rather than merging individual entries.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit clusters from project defaults; classic compute still requires an effective configuration.

entries.summary: Choose email recipients and pipeline events that trigger notifications.
details: Each notification block pairs email_recipients with alerts. A per-pipeline list replaces the inherited list.

entries.summary: Select pipeline events that should send this notification.
details: Use event names such as on-update-success, on-update-failure, on-update-fatal-failure or on-flow-failure.

entries.summary: Choose who receives this pipeline notification.
details: Provide email addresses for the selected alerts. Recipients belong to this notification block, not to the whole job.

entries.summary: Attach compute tags to a classic pipeline.
details: These are pipeline compute tags, separate from Unity Catalog table tags on write actions. Serverless tags come from the compute policy.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit tags by mapping key from project defaults.

entries.summary: Enable Photon for classic pipeline compute.
details: This setting is ignored when serverless is enabled. It does not select the pipeline runtime channel.
entries.unsetBehavior: When unset here, the project-default value applies. If neither level sets this key, only a documented LHP or platform default applies; omission is not the same as an explicit value.

entries.summary: Override event-log configuration for this pipeline.
details: An object replaces the lhp.yaml event_log configuration for this pipeline; false explicitly disables event logging here.
entries.unsetBehavior: Use the project event-log behavior unless the pipeline configuration inherits an override.

entries.summary: Choose the identity used to execute this pipeline.
details: Supply the supported identity mapping, for example service_principal_name. This controls execution identity, while permissions control who can access the pipeline.
entries.unsetBehavior: When unset here, the project-default value applies. If neither level sets this key, only a documented LHP or platform default applies; omission is not the same as an explicit value.

entries.summary: Grant access to this pipeline.
details: Each entry needs a permission level and exactly one identity: a user, group or service principal. An explicit list replaces the inherited list.

entries.summary: Choose the access level for this identity.
details: Select an access level supported for this resource, such as CAN_VIEW or CAN_MANAGE. Give the identity the access it needs to perform its role.

entries.summary: Identify a user by their email address.
details: Set only one of user_name, group_name and service_principal_name in an entry.

entries.summary: Grant this permission to a workspace group.
details: Use the group name, and leave user_name and service_principal_name unset in this entry.

entries.summary: Grant this permission to a service principal.
details: Use the service principal application ID, not its display name; leave the other identity fields unset.

entries.summary: Name the event-log table for this pipeline.
details: This is part of a full per-pipeline event-log override; the object replaces the project-level event-log setting.

entries.summary: Choose the catalog for this pipeline’s event-log table.
details: Provide this together with schema and name in the custom event-log override.

entries.summary: Choose the schema for this pipeline’s event-log table.
details: This is event-log storage, separate from the catalog/schema for business output tables.

entries.summary: Identify the role of this pipeline cluster.
details: Use the pipeline cluster label, commonly default. It distinguishes this cluster definition from other compute roles.

entries.summary: Choose the cloud instance type for cluster workers.
details: Use a node type available in your workspace’s cloud and region. This is a classic-compute setting.

entries.summary: Choose the cloud instance type for the cluster driver.
details: The driver coordinates the Spark workload. This setting is separate from the worker node type.

entries.summary: Apply a workspace compute policy to this cluster.
details: Use the policy identifier. The policy can constrain which other cluster settings are allowed.

entries.summary: Set the lower worker limit for classic cluster autoscaling.
details: Keep this no greater than max_workers; the autoscaler can resize within the configured bounds.

entries.summary: Set the upper worker limit for classic cluster autoscaling.
details: Keep this no smaller than min_workers. The upper bound limits how far compute can scale out.

entries.summary: Choose the autoscaling mode for the pipeline cluster.
details: Use the mode supported by your pipeline configuration; ENHANCED is the common pipeline autoscaling mode.
